title: How an Electric Drill Works in 60 Seconds 🔩⚡ #shorts
description:
A cordless drill's motor can spin around 20,000 RPM, far too fast and weak to drive a screw. A planetary gearbox trades that speed for torque, a spring-loaded clutch slips when the screw is tight, and a three-jaw chuck grips the bit dead center. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#drill #engineering #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: The motor inside a cordless drill can spin about *20,000 times* a minute.

steps.label: Trigger
steps.text: Squeeze the *trigger* harder, and more battery *power* flows to the motor.

steps.label: Gears
steps.text: That's too fast to drive a screw, so small *planet gears* slow it down and multiply the *torque*.

steps.label: Speeds
steps.text: A switch picks the gear: about *450 RPM* for power, or up to *2,000* for speed.

steps.label: Clutch
steps.text: The numbered collar is a *clutch*. When the screw gets tight, spring-loaded balls *slip* so you don't strip it.

steps.label: Chuck
steps.text: Up front, three *jaws* close together to grip the bit *dead center*.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Spin, gear down, *grip*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
